items.html: Rubio said Tuesday the US is open to talks with Iran during UNGA week but no meeting is arranged yet, while reiterating "Iran can never have a nuclear weapon." (Al Arabiya English)

items.title: Trump told the UN General Assembly he has "a big decision to make" — a deal that lets Iran "rebuild," or to "annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly" — and said he expects a deal "right after the election" because Iran is "waiting to see how I do in the midterm election."
items.html: Trump told the UN General Assembly he has "a big decision to make" — a deal that lets Iran "rebuild," or to "annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly" — and said he expects a deal "right after the election" because Iran is "waiting to see how I do in the midterm election." The transcript sets no deadline and no ultimatum date: he framed it as a choice still to be made, asked all nations to join "the complete economic isolation of Iran," and repeated that "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon." Iran's delegation walked out as he described the war; the Armed Forces General Staff answered that his words were "a sign of their strategic desperation" and promised strikes "more crushing and less predictable" than earlier ones. (Roll Call Factba.se transcript, NBC News, Al Jazeera)

items.title: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held about three hours of talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi at the UN on Tuesday, with Qatari mediators shuttling between the delegations — the first in-person contact since June.
items.html: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held about three hours of talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi at the UN on Tuesday, with Qatari mediators shuttling between the delegations — the first in-person contact since June. Accounts differ on the format: Witkoff said mediators "shuttled between" the sides, Trump called it a "very good meeting" and said another was expected "in the very near future," and the White House later clarified that Trump himself did not attend. Iranian state media said the US asked for the meeting and that Araghchi restated Tehran's conditions: an end to the naval blockade, release of frozen assets and an end to the war on all fronts. (Al Jazeera, Guardian)

items.title: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards spokesman said Tehran has "toughened" its conditions for ending the war since the June memorandum collapsed — demanding the full $24 billion of frozen assets up front and adding an end to the blockade on Yemen — and Iran's foreign ministry said nothing new was conveyed in the New York talks.
items.html: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards spokesman said Tehran has "toughened" its conditions for ending the war since the June memorandum collapsed — demanding the full $24 billion of frozen assets up front and adding an end to the blockade on Yemen — and Iran's foreign ministry said nothing new was conveyed in the New York talks. Hossein Mohebi told AFP that "we believe we have won this war." The line sits alongside the Hormuz-reopening offer already on the thread rather than replacing it: an official told Reuters the strait could reopen within seven days if the US eases pressure. (Naharnet, AFP, Guardian)

items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Tehran has the technological infrastructure to build missiles of "significantly longer ranges" and claimed a new missile recently hit a US aircraft carrier from about 500 km, damaging but not disabling it.
items.html: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Tehran has the technological infrastructure to build missiles of "significantly longer ranges" and claimed a new missile recently hit a US aircraft carrier from about 500 km, damaging but not disabling it. Spokesman Hossein Mohebbi told IRNA that a political decision is still needed on producing longer-range missiles; the US has not confirmed any strike on a carrier, so the hit is an IRGC claim only. (Africanews, AP)

items.title: The Guardian reports that fewer than five identifiable tankers a day are making it through the Strait of Hormuz, against Trump's UN claim that the US Navy has "escorted more than 1 billion barrels of oil" out of it and is taking "22, 25, 30, 32 and 37 ships out" each day.
items.html: The Guardian reports that fewer than five identifiable tankers a day are making it through the Strait of Hormuz, against Trump's UN claim that the US Navy has "escorted more than 1 billion barrels of oil" out of it and is taking "22, 25, 30, 32 and 37 ships out" each day. The two figures are not reconciled by any published data; the Guardian notes US Navy estimates are much higher than identifiable-tanker counts, commercial shipping remains below pre-war levels, and intermittent attacks continue. (Guardian, Roll Call Factba.se transcript)

items.title: Russia struck Ukraine overnight into Tuesday with its largest barrage since the Duma vote closed — at least 8 killed, 37 wounded across 22 locations, including a ballistic-missile hit on Dnipro's Interpipe industrial plant that killed 4 employees and halted production.
items.html: Russia struck Ukraine overnight into Tuesday with its largest barrage since the Duma vote closed — at least 8 killed, 37 wounded across 22 locations, including a ballistic-missile hit on Dnipro's Interpipe industrial plant that killed 4 employees and halted production. Ukraine's air force logged a mix of Oniks, Iskander-M/ S-400/KN-23, four Kalibr cruise missiles, eight Banderol/Dan-T weapons and 212 drones; Chernihiv region separately lost power to nearly 100,000 residents. (Kyiv Independent, Al Jazeera)

items.title: Zelensky arrived in New York for UN General Assembly week with a Trump meeting scheduled tonight and a Ukraine drone-technology deal ready to sign
items.html: Zelensky arrived in New York for UN General Assembly week with a Trump meeting scheduled tonight and a Ukraine drone-technology deal ready to sign, part of roughly 20 meetings planned this week; he met Macron Monday on air-defense systems. (Kyiv Independent)

items.title: Zelensky and Trump met at the UN on Tuesday — their first meeting since July — and discussed an energy-infrastructure ceasefire, winter support, Patriot production licences and a possible three-way meeting with Putin, but announced no agreement.
items.html: Zelensky and Trump met at the UN on Tuesday — their first meeting since July — and discussed an energy-infrastructure ceasefire, winter support, Patriot production licences and a possible three-way meeting with Putin, but announced no agreement. Zelensky said Ukraine is "ready for energy ceasefire" if Moscow accepts the same terms and that the US "will share it with Russians"; Trump said "I think we're going to make a deal" and, in his UN speech, that the war will end "more quickly than people understand," while telling reporters Ukraine's refinery strikes were "a serious hit on the price of diesel." Zelensky said he had no "very concrete answer" on Patriot systems. (Kyiv Independent, AP via Business Standard)

items.title: The EU removed Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list on Tuesday while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 individuals and companies for 36 months instead of six.
items.html: The EU removed Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list on Tuesday while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 individuals and companies for 36 months instead of six. The delistings — pushed by France (Usmanov, tied to a prisoner-exchange deal involving Azerbaijan) and Luxembourg (Fridman, who is suing it for $16bn) — were the price of the unanimity needed before the end-of-Tuesday deadline; Zelensky and Foreign Minister Sybiha called it unacceptable and "shameful." (Guardian, Kyiv Independent)

items.title: Ukrainian special forces hit the Kuibyshev oil refinery in Samara and another refinery in Bashkortostan overnight into Tuesday, Zelensky said; Samara's governor reported one killed and four wounded.
items.html: Ukrainian special forces hit the Kuibyshev oil refinery in Samara and another refinery in Bashkortostan overnight into Tuesday, Zelensky said; Samara's governor reported one killed and four wounded. Russia's Defence Ministry said it downed 297 Ukrainian drones over 14 regions that night. Trump has urged Kyiv to stop refinery strikes because of diesel prices; Zelensky said Ukraine would stop if Russia stops attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure. (AP via Business Standard)

items.title: As many as 169 people were reported killed in Yemen in three days as Houthi and Saudi-backed government forces fought for the Kahboub mountains and other heights over the Red Sea coast, with thousands fleeing.
items.html: As many as 169 people were reported killed in Yemen in three days as Houthi and Saudi-backed government forces fought for the Kahboub mountains and other heights over the Red Sea coast, with thousands fleeing. Houthi officials told AFP at least 118 died in clashes and Saudi air and artillery strikes on Taiz, al-Jawf, Marib and Saada since Sunday; government sources said at least 36 died on their side. The Houthis said a Saudi strike on Mocha on Tuesday killed six civilians, including two children, and one on a prison in al-Jawf killed nine detainees — claims Saudi Arabia has not confirmed. (Guardian)

items.title: Yemen's government forces said they took full control of Mount Qarfan in southern Taiz on Tuesday, killing five Houthi fighters and wounding 20, according to the Taiz military axis chief of staff.
items.html: Yemen's government forces said they took full control of Mount Qarfan in southern Taiz on Tuesday, killing five Houthi fighters and wounding 20, according to the Taiz military axis chief of staff. The Houthis had not commented; the peak gives fire control over valleys between the ash-Shamaytaun and al-Waziiya districts as the Houthis push to control the wider Kahboub range, which would cut their coastal gains off from Aden's hinterland. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: Britain will send an RAF Voyager tanker to refuel Saudi fighter jets in "defensive air-to-air refuelling," Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday, after Saudi Arabia requested air-defence support.
items.html: Britain will send an RAF Voyager tanker to refuel Saudi fighter jets in "defensive air-to-air refuelling," Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday, after Saudi Arabia requested air-defence support. Burnham called the arrangement "time-limited" and said the UK will not join the war directly; the Ministry of Defence said it builds on UK air-defence equipment and personnel already deployed in the kingdom. Announced Monday 09-21, reported through Tuesday and Wednesday. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: Saudi Arabia's King Salman called the suspected Houthi drone targeting of Mecca a "heinous crime" and a provocation against Muslims worldwide, in remarks to the cabinet on Tuesday reported by the Saudi Press Agency.
items.html: Saudi Arabia's King Salman called the suspected Houthi drone targeting of Mecca a "heinous crime" and a provocation against Muslims worldwide, in remarks to the cabinet on Tuesday reported by the Saudi Press Agency. The Houthis deny targeting Mecca — leader Abdel-Malik al-Houthi called the Saudi claim "a heinous lie" last week — and it is a rare direct intervention by the king, whose son the crown prince normally leads day-to-day affairs. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: The foreign ministers of the G7 — the UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the US — condemned "in the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes" by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia and called on Iran to stop arming the group, in a statement issued Monday after an informal meeting at the UN.
items.html: The foreign ministers of the G7 — the UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the US — condemned "in the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes" by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia and called on Iran to stop arming the group, in a statement issued Monday after an informal meeting at the UN. They urged the Houthis to stop attacks on civilian shipping and return to the political process. (Al Jazeera)

items.title: Ethiopian federal drone and fighter-jet strikes on the Tigrayan town of Alamata killed at least 14 civilians and injured 22 on Tuesday, Tigray's authorities said, in more than 21 strikes beginning around 3:30am local time that hit two unoccupied secondary schools, the mayor said.
items.html: Ethiopian federal drone and fighter-jet strikes on the Tigrayan town of Alamata killed at least 14 civilians and injured 22 on Tuesday, Tigray's authorities said, in more than 21 strikes beginning around 3:30am local time that hit two unoccupied secondary schools, the mayor said. The BBC has not verified the claims and the government has not commented. Separately, the US State Department condemned a Monday drone strike on a Catholic convoy carrying food aid in the region and called for an investigation. (BBC News)

items.title: South Sudan's President Salva Kiir dissolved the transitional government, removed all five vice-presidents and dissolved parliament on Tuesday, three months before the country's first-ever election on 22 December.
items.html: South Sudan's President Salva Kiir dissolved the transitional government, removed all five vice-presidents and dissolved parliament on Tuesday, three months before the country's first-ever election on 22 December. He signed election-law amendments the day before, stays in office "with full constitutional powers" until a president is sworn in, and reappointed some ministers and governors as caretakers; the opposition leader Riek Machar is under house arrest on treason charges, and soldiers blocked access to ministries in Juba. (BBC News, Al Jazeera)

items.title: Gaza's Health Ministry reported four Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in 24 hours to Tuesday, plus one who died of earlier wounds, and 25 injured; the ministry's post-ceasefire toll stands at 1,399 killed and 4,863 wounded.
items.html: Gaza's Health Ministry reported four Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in 24 hours to Tuesday, plus one who died of earlier wounds, and 25 injured; the ministry's post-ceasefire toll stands at 1,399 killed and 4,863 wounded. Palestinian media said Israeli drone strikes on Tuesday evening in Gaza City's Tuffah neighbourhood killed three more, and counted it as the 348th consecutive day of ceasefire violations. Figures are the Health Ministry's and local reporting; the incidents are not independently verified. (Palestine Information Center, WAFA, Antiwar.com)

items.title: Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland's Premier Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed a security agreement at the UN letting the US "modernise and expand" Pituffik Space Base, establish new bases at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, and fly and operate across Greenland's territory, waters and undersea approaches.
items.html: Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland's Premier Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed a security agreement at the UN letting the US "modernise and expand" Pituffik Space Base, establish new bases at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, and fly and operate across Greenland's territory, waters and undersea approaches. No non-NATO country may set up military installations or a persistent presence without unanimous approval by Denmark, Greenland and the US, investors from sensitive sectors outside NATO and the EU are barred, and the pact has no end date; Denmark and Greenland keep sovereignty, and an independent Greenland would remain in NATO. Trump described it as giving the US "permanent control over security"; Frederiksen called it "a deal that can last forever." (Al Jazeera, NBC News)

items.title: Trump told the UN his administration is "seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba," which he called "a failed state" that "will fall," and said Marco Rubio is "deep into negotiations with Cuba"; the Cuban delegation walked out of the hall.
items.html: Trump told the UN his administration is "seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba," which he called "a failed state" that "will fall," and said Marco Rubio is "deep into negotiations with Cuba"; the Cuban delegation walked out of the hall. He also called the January capture of Nicolás Maduro "proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere," and met Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodríguez on the sidelines, their first meeting since Maduro's seizure. (NBC News, Roll Call Factba.se transcript, Guardian)

items.title: OpenAI brought voice-based agentic features to the ChatGPT mobile app, letting Plus and Pro subscribers trigger workflows — drafting documents, summarizing Slack messages, building sites — from the phone's Work tab and switch between text and voice mid-conversation
items.html: OpenAI brought voice-based agentic features to the ChatGPT mobile app, letting Plus and Pro subscribers trigger workflows — drafting documents, summarizing Slack messages, building sites — from the phone's Work tab and switch between text and voice mid-conversation — Free and Go users get plugins and connected apps instead; the rollout extends to mobile what OpenAI shipped to desktop after July's GPT-Live launch, arriving ahead of DevDay on 09-29. (TechCrunch)

items.title: Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced legislation to permanently ban artificial superintelligence, pause development of the most advanced AI systems until new federal rules exist, and create a Department of Artificial Intelligence
items.html: Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced legislation to permanently ban artificial superintelligence, pause development of the most advanced AI systems until new federal rules exist, and create a Department of Artificial Intelligence — advanced systems would then need federal approval before deployment, with penalties of up to 20 years in prison in some cases; employees of OpenAI and Google DeepMind endorsed it in their personal capacity, and the bill faces long odds in the Republican-controlled Congress. (AP via ABC News)

items.title: OpenAI is giving Ukraine's government access to its Daybreak cyber-defense program to help protect civilian infrastructure, the first active conflict zone to get that level of access
items.html: OpenAI is giving Ukraine's government access to its Daybreak cyber-defense program to help protect civilian infrastructure, the first active conflict zone to get that level of access — working with Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation, it will supply tools to find software vulnerabilities and test fixes; Ukraine's CERT-UA handled nearly 6,000 incidents in 2025. It was announced on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. (OpenAI, AI Weekly)

items.title: Sanders and Casar's own release, beyond the "pause," would set a "corporate death penalty" for entities that violate the ban and up to 20 years in prison for individuals, bar any AI capable of "overthrowing the federal government," and set US policy to pursue international agreements and export controls against superintelligence anywhere in the world
items.html: Sanders and Casar's own release, beyond the "pause," would set a "corporate death penalty" for entities that violate the ban and up to 20 years in prison for individuals, bar any AI capable of "overthrowing the federal government," and set US policy to pursue international agreements and export controls against superintelligence anywhere in the world — the bill text, one-pager and section-by-section summary are posted on Sanders's own site; Sanders: "When the future of humanity is at stake, we cannot let a handful of Big Tech CEOs write their own rules." No Congress.gov bill number had been indexed as of this afternoon. (Sen. Bernie Sanders, primary)

items.title: OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei told the UN Security Council, in its first meeting devoted specifically to AI slipping beyond human control, that AI's risks are serious and that its biggest decisions cannot be left to the labs alone — Amodei: "If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole"; Altman: "If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. items.html: OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei told the UN Security Council, in its first meeting devoted specifically to AI slipping beyond human control, that AI's risks are serious and that its biggest decisions cannot be left to the labs alone — Amodei: "If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole"; Altman: "If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people they serve." Altman, briefing in person, also said the current moment "calls for extreme care" since an increasingly automated development process could let AI's pace of improvement "accelerate rapidly," and repeated that "the industry must not accept too much technological risk just because the benefits are too great and important to slow down" — an endorsement of the pacing proposal Amodei made in mid-September. Amodei and Hugging Face's Clément Delangue briefed remotely; French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot chaired; Council members including the US and China were expected to speak after the briefers. No Council product (resolution or statement) had emerged as of this writing, and wire coverage had not confirmed whether DeepSeek and Moonshot, both reported invited, actually spoke. Yoshua Bengio, co-chair of the UN's Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, told the same session "the dangers are real and imminent." (Reuters, primary, via Yahoo Finance, AFP, primary, via Le Figaro)

items.html: A University of Illinois Chicago trial of "Coach Lumen," a voice-based AI coach delivering problem-solving therapy, posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov on 09-23: at 18 weeks, participants coached by the AI improved more than a delayed-treatment control, and those coached by a human improved somewhat more than the AI-coached group on most measures, in unadjusted registry means. On the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale's distress total, the mean change was −5.85 for the AI-coached arm (97 completers), −7.33 for human coaching (48) and −2.76 for the delayed-treatment control (49); the session-level PHQ-9 and GAD-7 changes were −4.56, −5.81 and −1.63, and −4.53, −5.60 and −0.80, in the same order. Three cautions from the record itself: the registry posts descriptive means only, with no between-group tests or confidence intervals; the trial's pre-specified primary outcome was change in a functional-MRI activation measure, on which the arms are not visibly different, with the symptom scales all listed as secondary; and the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 figures come from smaller session-level samples (72, 43 and 30). The 200-person Phase 2 ran 2023 to April 2025 and is NIMH-funded with Penn State, Washington University and Stanford as collaborators; whether a journal paper exists was not checked. Academic, with a human comparator and a delayed-treatment control, it is the kind of evidence this thread asks whether the field can produce. (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05603923)

items.title: US business activity grew at its fastest pace in more than five years in September, S&P Global's flash PMI showed Wednesday: the composite output index rose to 58.4 from 56.0, services reached 58.7 and manufacturing 57.0, while input costs rose at the steepest rate in four years.
items.html: US business activity grew at its fastest pace in more than five years in September, S&P Global's flash PMI showed Wednesday: the composite output index rose to 58.4 from 56.0, services reached 58.7 and manufacturing 57.0, while input costs rose at the steepest rate in four years. Employment grew at a pace not seen for over four years and backlogs of work rose at the sharpest rate since May 2022; S&P Global's Chris Williamson said the data point to annualized growth of around 5%, described "some of the most severe supply chain bottlenecks" of the survey's history outside the pandemic, and called the build-up in pricing power "a worry for the inflation outlook." Treasury yields jumped on the release: as of about 10am ET the 10-year was up more than 7bp at roughly 5.04% and the 2-year up more than 8bp at 4.858%, against 4.96% and 4.71% at Tuesday's close, while the S&P 500 was down 0.3% and the Nasdaq down 0.5%. (S&P Global Flash US PMI, CNBC live updates)

interpretation.mechanism: A composite PMI at a five-year high with input costs at a four-year high and rising backlogs is the demand-led inflation story that Fed presidents Musalem, Goolsbee and Collins made in words this week. It raises the odds the Fed keeps hiking after 09-16, and higher expected policy rates lift the 10-year, which is why yields jumped 7bp on the release. The long end has mostly followed oil and the Fed rather than Treasury's own buyback in September, and this is the Fed leg.

items.title: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped more than 14 basis points Wednesday afternoon to 5.116% — its highest since July 2007 and its biggest one-day move in nearly 18 months — after a Treasury auction of 5-year notes drew weak demand and Fed Governor Michael Barr said "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed" to bring inflation to target.
items.html: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped more than 14 basis points Wednesday afternoon to 5.116% — its highest since July 2007 and its biggest one-day move in nearly 18 months — after a Treasury auction of 5-year notes drew weak demand and Fed Governor Michael Barr said "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed" to bring inflation to target. The auction priced at a 5.033% yield against a six-auction average of 4.186%, with indirect bidders (a group that includes foreign central banks) taking just 54% against a 65% average — "a poor auction with Treasury trying to sell paper into a weak market," per One Point BFG Wealth Partners' Peter Boockvar. The 2-year yield jumped more than 12bp to 4.906%, its highest since May 2024, and the 30-year gained more than 10bp to 5.41%. CME FedWatch's odds of an October 25bp hike rose to about 73% from 55% a day earlier and under 10% a month ago. The S&P 500 was down about 0.7% and the Nasdaq about 1% intraday as of 3pm ET, both off Tuesday's record closes; the average 30-year mortgage rate rose 9bp to 7.26% (Mortgage News Daily), the highest in close to two years. (CNBC, Yahoo Finance)

interpretation.mechanism: A weak 5-year note auction is a direct test of this thread's own question — whether Treasury can keep selling duration at yields the market finds attractive while the Fed is still hiking — and today it failed that test: the auction priced 5.033% against a 4.186% six-auction average, with indirect (largely foreign-official) bidders taking only 54% against a 65% average, i.e. the usual buyer base showed up in smaller size and had to be paid up to clear the issue. Fed Governor Barr's same-day "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed" landed on top of that weak demand and pushed CME FedWatch's October-hike odds from 55% to 70% in a single session, which is the reaction-function logic (hawkish talk plus strong data or weak demand moves the long end) this thread has tracked all month.

scenarios.direction: The 10-year holds above 5.1% into Thursday's jobless claims and SoftBank's bond pricing, and a weak claims read or another hawkish Fed voice pushes it toward 5.2%, raising the funding cost of SoftBank's own OpenAI bond before it prices and tightening financing conditions for the wider AI-debt stack this thread and Son All-In both track.
scenarios.why: Every external-driver move this thread has logged this month has held through at least the next session rather than round-tripping intraday, and SoftBank's own tranche guidance (up to 9.875% on its longest notes) already prices in a higher-for-longer path.
scenarios.precedent: 09-16 to 09-18: the 10-year cleared 5% after the Fed hike and closed at a fresh 2007-era high on 09-18, extending rather than reversing over three sessions (Treasury's Long-End Defense 09-18 entry).

scenarios.direction: The move partly reverses by Thursday's close if claims data comes in soft or oil resumes its decline, the way this month's spikes have repeatedly given back part of a hawkish-data move within a session or two rather than holding the full jump.
scenarios.why: A single weak 5-year auction is not unprecedented and this thread has already logged several same-week reversals (09-17's oil-driven pullback from above 5% to 4.93% is the clearest instance).
scenarios.precedent: 09-17: the 10-year eased from an intraday high above 5% to a 4.93% close the same day CNBC tied an equity rebound to falling oil, on Treasury's Long-End Defense's own 09-17 entry.

items.title: Tigrayan forces seized airports across the Tigray region and launched an offensive against federal positions in the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions early Wednesday, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's adviser Getachew Reda said; Tigray's authorities say they are fighting a "defensive war" against a federal "invasion."
items.html: Tigrayan forces seized airports across the Tigray region and launched an offensive against federal positions in the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions early Wednesday, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's adviser Getachew Reda said; Tigray's authorities say they are fighting a "defensive war" against a federal "invasion." Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to three northern Tigray airports, residents of Mekelle told the BBC that local forces took over its airport from federal police, and clashes were reported in Afar at Abala and Berahle. AFP reported that humanitarian staff in Afar said fighting between the TPLF and federal forces broke out at Abala and Erebti late Tuesday, and a foreign security source said the TPLF controlled Abala. The fighting comes three days after the Tigray People's Liberation Front announced an alliance with six other armed groups to remove Abiy's government, and a day after Tigrayan authorities said federal strikes killed at least 14 in Alamata; the BBC could not independently verify either side's account of who attacked first. The International Crisis Group's Alan Boswell said "if we're not all the way back into something like a full war, we are very, very close," and that Eritrea's alignment with the TPLF threatens to make it regional. (Al Jazeera, AFP, BBC News, Africanews, AFP)

items.html: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, addressing the UN General Assembly, answered Trump's speech directly: "The US president described us as terrorists.
